projection: Mercator (d3.geoMercator, spherical), north up; scale 3666.930 = 64 px per degree of longitude, center [83.25,27.6] at pixel [480,360]

sources.what: Natural Earth 10m Shaded Relief, low-res edition (SR_LR.tif, v2.0.0, 16200x8100, 45 px/degree), grayscale hillshade cropped to 72-95E 19-36N
Natural Earth 10m rivers + lake centerlines (ne_10m_rivers_lake_centerlines), cut to the same box

note: Relief is real data, not drawn: the blue tone is the Natural Earth hillshade (shadowed slopes inked, lit slopes left as paper) plus a tone of local ruggedness measured from the same hillshade, so darker means steeper. No elevation model was used, so tone is not height: the high Himalaya is darkest because it is the most rugged ground, and flat ground (the plain, and any sea) is bare paper. Rivers and relief only: no country, admin or boundary layer was loaded, no coastline is stroked, and there is no text. The tone is laid in 5 flat tints, as a screen print would be. anchors.india is at 80.1E 24.6N, not the 81E 25.5N first asked for: that point (anchors_as_asked.india) sits on the Yamuna just above its confluence with the Ganga, so both rivers would run through the word; the anchor given is the nearest open paper, just south of the Yamuna. anchors.nepal is on the darkest part of the plate, so a label there needs a paper-coloured face or a paper casing. kathmandu and delhi are end points for arrows and are not marked on the plate. Drawn by design/map.mjs; data cut once by design/map_prep.py.
